correctness.rationale: The frozen proof's Frobenius certificate fails: G mod 7=(z−3)^2(z²−z−1), and its own discriminant is divisible by 7. The archived test counts factors with multiplicity, so it accepts the repeated linear factor without checking squarefreeness. The replacement proves the same arithmetic result using the good prime 13: G=z(z−5)(z²−4z+2) mod 13, with two different linear factors and quadratic discriminant 8 a nonsquare. The resulting transposition and the four-cycle at 5 force D4 inside the stabilizer of the rational resolvent pairing. Independently rewritten exact code under repairs/5 was run: it confirms the displayed homogeneous iterate/fixed-factor quotient, squarefreeness and point-factor irreducibility, the three cycle-sum remainder identities, the two quadratic discriminants, and the entire quartic resolvent and both good-prime tests. The three irreducible sum polynomials have disjoint roots and the degree ratios are all three; each sum identifies exactly one cycle, so its stabilizer equals the setwise cycle stabilizer. This checks the arithmetic descent for unordered cycles, rather than assuming point fields are cycle fields. The frozen files were not executed or modified.
residual_risks: The exact certificate pertains to the characteristic-zero moduli map, not twists or full point-field normal closures. It is not formal verification.
